bc_main_wall_4.blurb: Main Wall sits at the heart of Glen Lake Crag, a small basalt cliff west of Victoria on Vancouver Island. Its ten sport routes run from about 5.6 to 5.11, with most of the weight in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, so it suits a mixed group better than a hard-only wall. The face leans back just short of vertical, and the weathered basalt gives friction, edges and flakes. Its neighbour, the Karate Kid wall, is immediately to the side, which makes it easy to string a short day together. Expect a quick walk up a small ravine from the road, and think about a helmet since the top of the crag has loose rock.

bc_camas_wall.blurb: Camas Wall is the lowest wall on the right side of Glen Lake Crag, a basalt crag about ten kilometres from Victoria on Vancouver Island, and a big oak at its foot makes it easy to spot. It holds ten sport routes, mostly in the 5.10 and 5.11 range with one easier line and one 5.12, so it is the harder, more focused corner of an otherwise moderate crag. The face is a touch under vertical, and the weathered basalt offers friction, edges and flakes. Reaching it takes a short uphill walk from the road past a fire hydrant, then a trail up a small ravine.

bc_the_turret.blurb: The Turret is a small, short crag in the Red Tail Group of Skaha Bluffs near Penticton, perched on a grassy bench on top of The Fortress. It has ten routes, six sport and four trad, with most in the 5.10 range and a handful pushing 5.11 and 5.12, plus one or two easier lines. The setting is the main draw, with wide views over Skaha Lake and the town. It sits well off the busiest trails, so it can be a quiet fallback when the lower walls are crowded. A simple way to get there is to lead something on The Fortress and then stroll across the bench.

bc_plum_wall.blurb: Plum Wall is a stretch of The Fortress at Skaha Bluffs, above Penticton in the Okanagan. Ten routes, seven sport and three trad, start around 5.9 and climb through 5.10 to about 5.11, with half of them at 5.11. A couple of the best moderate lines at Skaha are found here, so it draws steady traffic. To reach it, follow the main trail to the Fortress, pass the Ramparts, then double back left on the upper path along the cliff base; a saskatoon bush beside the path marks the start.
